06acebdc72.q: What caused the 2008 financial crisis and what solutions were implemented to fix the system?
06acebdc72.a: The catalyst for 2008 was mortgage-backed securities. Rules around mortgages were relaxed, allowing no-doc loans where people didn't need to prove income. Financial institutions then created derivatives and leveraged bets against these securities multiple times over, exponentially increasing risk. When the crisis hit, instead of letting institutions fail naturally, governments worldwide printed money and monetized losses by buying assets, kicking the can down the road rather than resetting the system.
